chunks: And Hammad narrated from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام:

He was asked about two men between whom there was a slave, and one of them emancipated his share. He عليه السلام said: "If he was acting to cause harm, he will be required to emancipate all of him. Otherwise, the slave is to be made to work for the other half."

key_terms.اسْتُسْعِيَ: the slave is made to work to earn payment
key_terms.عَبْدٌ: a slave jointly owned by two parties
key_terms.فَأَعْتَقَ: then he emancipated or set free
key_terms.كُلِّفَ: he is legally required or obligated
key_terms.مُضَارًّا: acting with intent to cause harm

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one co-owner frees his share of a jointly owned slave?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding shared ownership of a slave when one partner frees only his portion. If the act was done maliciously to harm the co-owner, the emancipator must free the slave completely; otherwise, the slave must earn the value of the remaining share.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3439 - Hammad narrated from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdullah (as), that he was asked about two men who jointly owned a slave, and one of them freed his share.
Imam (as) said: "If he did so with the intent of causing harm, he will be required to free the slave completely. Otherwise, the slave must work to pay off the value of the remaining half."
